items.transcript: Here's everything I did and made to help one of my kids move into a new home, and I didn't just bring a housewarming gift. I came ready to roll up my sleeves. Before the furniture arrived, I opened the windows and got to work on all those little jobs that are so much easier to do before move-in day. Of course, I brought along my new book, Homemaking with Babs. You'll see why. I started by making a few of my favorite DIY cleaners. They're simple to make, use ingredients you probably already have at home, and are perfect for tackling all those little jobs around the house. The carpet had a few old stains, so I used my homemade carpet cleaner and gave those spots a little attention. You'd be surprised what you can remove with a few simple ingredients. The showerhead needed some help, so I cleaned away the mineral buildup and got that water flowing again. Another one of my favorite little tricks, write the paint color of the room behind the switch plate. When you need a touch-up, you'll know exactly what color to use. Then I worked my way through the appliances. I pulled out the dishwasher filter and gave it a good cleaning. It's one of those parts of your home that's easy to forget about, but food and buildup collect in there, so it needs a little attention every so often. And that's really the thing. These aren't just tips for moving into a new home. They're things we should all be doing to take care of the homes we live in. Homemaking with Babs walks you through what needs to be done and, just as importantly, when to do it. Next, the garbage disposal. I made my cleaning slushie and gave it a whirl. Surprisingly, ours wasn't too bad, but imagine what could be lurking in yours. Don't forget the drain. That needs to be cleaned every so often too. Once the appliances were taken care of, I put a simmer pot on the stove. There's nothing like a beautiful seasonal scent filling the air to start making a new house feel like home. We even found a few ants. Before you call an exterminator, try this little trick. Borax and sugar with cotton balls. And finally, I gave the washer and dryer a good cleaning too. They're two appliances we depend on all the time, but don't always remember they need a little care themselves. I also like to use charcoal to help absorb unwanted smells and moisture. Place a few charcoal bags in closets, cabinets, the laundry room, or anywhere that could use a little freshening up. After 50 years of homemaking, I put everything I know into Homemaking with Babs, the owner's manual your home should have come with.

items.transcript: At 77, here are the household tricks I wish I knew at 30. Use borax and sugar to get rid of ants. Works better than any $500 exterminator. Use Elmer's glue, baking soda, and contact lens solution to clean all those hard-to-reach areas in your car. Use white wine to get rid of red wine stains. Easy as that. Just blot with cold water and let dry. Use charcoal to control moisture and odor in all parts of your home. items.transcript: Here's everything I did to help my daughter with four kids get her home ready for back to school. Every season gives us a fresh start. That's exactly how I organized my new book, Homemaking with Babs, by the seasons of the year. When transitioning to fall, things get very busy, so that's why it's important to plan ahead. An organized, clean refrig and freezer just makes everything feel lighter. We set up dinner bins for the week, added a few freezer meals, plus wellness cubes whenever someone's not feeling too well. It's all about simple systems that work and make life easier. And yes, we even made a stomach bug bucket, because 2 a.m. is not the time to be searching for supplies. That's real life. We used my five-bin declutter system to tackle the kids' rooms. It keeps you focused and keeps you moving. We also set up a designated area for weekly family meetings, a homework station, and after-school drop zones. And the most important part, everyone gets involved, which is woven throughout my book, because running a home shouldn't fall on just one person. So we practice shoes in the drop zone, lunchbox and water bottle in the sink, backpack hung up, homework where it belongs, chore charts, the laundry loop, even carrying baskets upstairs. Don't be afraid to test your systems with your family, walk through them together, and order Homemaking with Babs today.

items.caption: The Hot Spoon Trick for Bug Bites 👏 Place a spoon in hot water for a few minutes, then gently press it against a mosquito bite for a few seconds. The warmth reduces the itch by affecting the proteins involved in your body’s itch response.
items.transcript: Want to take the itchies out of those bug bites? After cleaning the bite with soap and water, just run a spoon under hot water, but don't make it too hot, and then take that spoon and press it on that bug bite, just gently, for a minute or two. It'll break down the protein that caused the itchiness, and you'll still have the bite, but you won't be scratching.
